The source array fetches the upstream tarball directly from the package's own declared GitHub repository using a tagged release. This file is a standard .gitignore file containing a single entry: *, which ignores all files in the directory. This is a common and harmless practice in AUR packages, particularly for -git packages where the repository is used to track only the PKGBUILD and related files, with all generated or downloaded content being ignored.

There are no security concerns with this file. It contains no executable code, no network requests, no obfuscation, and no suspicious commands. The * pattern simply tells Git to ignore all files in the directory during version control operations, which does not pose any risk to the system or users.

This PKGBUILD for `sshpilot` is a standard, clean Arch package definition. The source is fetched from the project's own upstream GitHub repository (`https://github.com/mfat/sshpilot`) using a versioned tag (`v${pkgver}.tar.gz`), and the sha256sum is properly pinned (not SKIP), so the downloaded tarball is verified against a known hash. The build process uses `arch-meson` and `meson install` into `$pkgdir`, which is entirely standard for a Python/GTK application using the Meson build system. There are no suspicious operations: no `curl`/`wget` to external/unrelated hosts, no `eval` or `base64` decoding, no obfuscated code, no file system manipulation outside the package scope, and no data exfiltration. The declared dependencies (Python, libadwaita, vte4, sshpass, python-paramiko, python-cryptography, etc.) are all appropriate and expected for an SSH connection manager with an integrated terminal. The blueprint-compiler and gtk-update-icon-cache dependencies are standard for compiling Blueprint UI definitions and refreshing icon caches.

The file is purely declarative metadata consumed by pacman/AUR tools.
